title: Armor of God and teach-back
materials: Paper labels or real gear: belt, vest, boots, trash-can-lid shield, helmet, foam sword

displayContent.headline: The armor of God
displayContent.body: Ephesians 6:13–17. As each piece goes on, match it to what it stands for.

prompts.text: Which piece matters most? Defend your answer.
prompts.answer: No single right answer. Two points worth raising: the sword is the only piece for attacking, and Roman soldiers could lock their shields together, so faith works best in a group.

prompts.text: What does Paul say to do right after putting on the armor?
prompts.answer: Pray at all times (verse 18), like a soldier’s radio back to headquarters.

prompts.text: Teach it back: pick one thing from tonight and explain it to the group in 30 seconds.
prompts.answer: Leader: note which boys can explain which items for the mentor.

leaderScript: Read Ephesians 6:13–17 while a volunteer is “suited up” with paper labels or real gear.
Press → for the answer key and R to show it.
Press → for the discussion question. Make each boy defend his answer.
Press → for verse 18, then → for the teach-back.

cells: The Spirit: the word of God

ifShortOnTime: Skip the suit-up: show the answer key, ask which piece matters most, and do the teach-back.
